ev_0007.summary: Figure is a quadrilateral A-D-C-B (AD top, DC right, CB bottom, BA left) with interior points E on BC and F on DC. Segments A-F, F-E, A-E and C-P cross inside, with unlabeled intersection point_08 at (681.9,433.4) where FE and CP meet. P lies on line CP (about 28 px short of its upper extension) and the dashed P-E chain runs from P down to E. No right-angle marks were verified by detect_right_angle_marker (0 markers). Computed slope of CP (~0.83) and PE (~-2.07) gives an angle of about 104 deg, so P-E is NOT perpendicular to CP and no right angle is submitted at P. The tool's reported perpendicular junctions at A, B, C, D, E, P have no square-mark ink and are not submitted. Segment endpoints overshooting a labelled vertex by <=9 px were snapped to that vertex; the C-P segment keeps its 28 px overhang beyond P.

evidence: label_error (M): Confirmed in the original. A label M sits directly below the crossing of segment PC (C to P) and segment FE (E to F), at roughly the midpoint of that crossing. The critic's 'below-left' placement is slightly off, since M is essentially directly below the crossing. Whether the render lacks M cannot be verified from the image provided, but the GES label list (A, B, C, D, E, F, P) also omits M, which is consistent with the critic.

other (stub at P): The original shows no perpendicular stub or overhang at P. CP starts cleanly at P on line AF, and AF runs through P without a tick. The absence is confirmed in the original. The stub in the render is not visible in the materials provided, so it rests on the critic and the GES note of a ~28 px overhang.

wrong_style (seg_09 dashed PE): The original's dashed PE uses fine, light dashes that look thinner than the solid edges (AB, AD, BC, DC, AE, FE, AF, PC). This supports the critic's observation that the dashes should be lighter. The render's actual stroke width is not visible to me, so the heaviness itself is unverified.
